Aiya, let me think through this year. I'm sitting here with my notebook — my husband is out checking the well pump — and I need to plan out the 18 mu.

**The main fields, wheat and maize (12 mu)**

The big piece of our land, 12 mu, is the wheat-maize rotation like most people in our village. My wheat is already in the ground from last October — I planted around October 10-12, which is when my mother-in-law always said is right. Seed was that Jimai variety the agro-shop sells, I bought enough for 12 mu, about 15 kg of seed per mu.

Before planting I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu (that's one bag of 15-15-15 plus some extra urea, maybe 3 bags total across two mu). When the wheat starts jointing around March, I'll topdress urea, maybe half a bag per mu — Wang-ge next door always does this and he gets good wheat. If it doesn't rain by then I'll have to run the well. Water costs money from the meter, so I try to irrigate only at jointing and again at heading, two times if the rain is okay, three if it's dry. Last year I got around 420 kg/mu, the year before 400, so I expect about the same.

After wheat harvest in early June, the maize has to go in FAST — within a few days. My husband and I use the no-till planter the village cooperative rents out, 30 yuan per mu. We plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid, cost is more than wheat seed but the yield is worth it. Maize I fertilize once as a base, about one bag of compound per mu, then topdress urea at knee-high stage. Maize mostly drinks the summer rain, but if July is dry I irrigate once or twice. I usually get 450-500 kg/mu.

**Stevia (3 mu)**

Stevia is my cash crop. The buying company signs with us in spring and sends seedlings in May. I put 3 mu because it's profitable if the price holds, but it needs a lot of work — weeding by hand, my sister-in-law helps. Fertilizer is the buyer's recommendation, I just follow what they say, about 30 kg urea per mu split over the season, plus compound before transplanting.

**Cabbage (1.5 mu) and eggplant (1.5 mu)**

The vegetable plot is near the house, easy to water. Cabbage goes in spring around late March, I start seedlings in the small greenhouse plastic. Vegetables eat a lot of fertilizer — I dump chicken manure in the fall, plus compound at transplant, plus urea when they're growing fast. Some we eat, most goes to the Quzhou town market on Sunday, my mother takes it. Eggplant the same way, transplant in early May, picks run all summer. Pesticide I use for cabbage worms and eggplant flea beetles — only when I see them, not on a schedule, the bottles are expensive.

**What I worry about this year**

Fertilizer prices went up again. Last year a bag of urea was almost 130 yuan. I might have to use a little less on the maize topdress if money is tight after paying for the wheat harvest machine. And my older boy is in school now so I can't count on him for field work like before. We'll manage.
